topic.title: Does a ₹3 lakh emergency fund in a savings account fall behind rising prices over 10 years

title: Your emergency fund is quietly losing buying power
description: A ₹3 lakh emergency fund in a savings account at an assumed 3% a year, against prices rising at an assumed 6% a year, for 10 years. Rates are assumptions, not assured. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Comment GROW if your fund sits idle

result_line1 'Your buying power slips by' sits directly above the template's large gap figure ₹1.3 L (b_final minus a_final, i.e. 5.4 L vs 4.0 L). Buying power actually falls from ₹3.0 L to ₹2.3 L, a loss of about ₹0.7 L, so the headline figure overstates the loss and contradicts result_line2 '25% of its value is gone' (₹1.3 L is about 43% of ₹3 L). Reword result_line1 to introduce the gap correctly, e.g. 'Prices pull ahead of savings by'.

Myth framing hides the emergency fund's purpose (liquidity and safety, not returns). Add a line such as 'Safety comes first' so the video does not imply the fund should chase returns; 'keep it working' risks reading as advice to invest an emergency fund. Reword end_line2 to stay illustrative.
